summary.oneLiner: A visionary Indian FMCG company with a strong consumer connect, holding market-leading positions in Fabric Care, Dishwashing and Household Insecticide categories.
summary.business: Jyothy Labs manufactures and markets Fast Moving Consumer Goods across Fabric Care, Dishwashing, Household Insecticide and Personal Care categories for Indian households, and through its Fabric Spa brand also provides laundry and dry-cleaning services. Products reach consumers pan-India (and in 19 countries via exports) through general trade, modern trade, e-commerce and quick-commerce channels.

currentContext.strengths: Market-leading brand positions: #1 Ujala Supreme in Fabric Whitener (since launch ~4 decades ago), #2 Exo Dishwash Bar in the Dishwash category by value, #2 Maxo Mosquito Repellent Coil by volume|Wide direct distribution reach — 4 million outlets where products are available, 1.4 million outlets under direct reach, 10,000+ channel partners|Net debt-free financial position with a substantial cash and bank balance (Rs 997 crore as of March 31, 2026), supporting continued investment capacity|Sustained brand investment via high-profile multi-channel campaigns (brand ambassadors including Vidya Balan, Kareena Kapoor, Keerthy Suresh, Nayanthara, Raashii Khanna and Manju Warrier) across TV, digital and OOH|Use of low unit packs (LUPs) to defend volume in rural/semi-urban markets against both unorganised local rivals and large competitors|Growing presence in modern trade, e-commerce and quick commerce, which grew 26% in FY26, widening reach to new urban consumers|R&D capability oriented towards green chemistry, automation and digital demand forecasting, supporting premiumisation and high-margin product development|Recognised employer (Great Place to Work Certified Feb 2025-Feb 2026; among India's top 50 Best Workplaces in Manufacturing 2026 and Best Workplaces in FMCG 2025), aiding talent retention
currentContext.strategies: Continued strengthening of the core business by listening to consumers and responding with agility to evolving needs, backed by fiscal discipline and execution excellence|Scaling up recent new product launches with greater focus on premium products, driving volume-led growth through innovation and distribution, supported by calibrated pricing|Maintaining brand investment intensity by integrating it into disciplined financial planning, to sustain strong consumer recall in a competitive market|Expanding direct retail reach (outlet additions) alongside deepening presence in Modern Trade, e-commerce and quick commerce channels to reach new urban consumers|Building Exo into a broader owned dishwash brand platform across formats, following Henkel's decision not to renew the Pril and Fa licence agreements beyond May 31, 2026|Using data-driven analytics to understand evolving consumer needs and strengthen consumer engagement|Scaling ESG focus with targeted environmental sustainability initiatives (Zero Liquid Discharge, solar installations, recycled packaging) alongside investment in people welfare and career progression|The Company maintains a formal Dividend Distribution Policy (adopted under SEBI Listing Regulation 43A, applicable to it as a top-500 listed company by market capitalisation) whose stated intent is to reward shareholders by sharing a portion of profits after retaining sufficient funds for the Company's growth; the Board's dividend recommendation each year weighs the circumstances and factors set out in that Policy rather than following a fixed formula.
currentContext.expansion: Jyothy Labs operates 23 manufacturing/processing facilities nationally (no international plants) supported by 32 depots and warehouses located pan-India and 3 R&D labs (Mumbai, Silvassa, Puducherry). The Company states capex on capacity expansion and upgradation of Rs 67 Crore during FY 2025-26, alongside continued investment in embracing advanced technologies and automation at its manufacturing units. On the sustainability/packaging side, during the year the Company completed the transition of the Exo Bar Rs 5 pack to a redesigned lightweight laminate, achieving an 11.3% reduction in plastic weight per unit versus the previous structure, and launched the new Exo Bar with Bio Enzymes range (3 variants) at the Rs 5 price point directly in this reduced-structure laminate. On energy, the Company reports a green solar energy capacity of 1,226 kW, renewable energy utilised of 15,60,056 kWh, and water savings of approximately 10% during FY26.
currentContext.mdna: Demand recovery in H2 FY26 aided by GST rate cuts and relative resilience in rural markets (good monsoon and government spending)|2X growth in liquid detergents powered Fabric Care's outperformance (8.1% value growth, 9.5% volume growth) within the segment|Dishwashing recorded 6% volume growth but a marginal 1.3% value decline, reflecting category-wide price corrections|Household Insecticide segment losses narrowed on an improved mix led by Liquid Vaporisers and new formats, moving the segment towards profitability|Raw material cost inflation could not be fully passed on to consumers, pressuring Gross Margin, EBITDA and PAT in FY26; geopolitical tensions added to the pressure|Modern Trade, e-commerce and quick commerce channels grew 26% in FY26, becoming an increasingly important growth and new-customer-acquisition driver versus traditional trade|For FY27, crude-linked input costs and geopolitical uncertainty may keep inflation elevated and affect consumer spending; rural demand may remain sensitive to farm incomes and monsoon outcomes|Industry-level: urban FMCG volume growth (4.6% in 2025) outpaced rural (3.6%), while overall Indian FMCG volume growth slowed to 4.1% in 2025 from 4.7% in 2024|GST 2.0 transition caused short-term disruption in Traditional Trade due to pricing/supply recalibration, while Modern Trade saw a sharp acceleration in Q3 FY26

risks.note: Business performance may be adversely affected by unfavourable macroeconomic conditions in domestic or global markets; mitigated via flexible strategies, prudent investments, focussed portfolio management and disciplined cost control.
Brand value may be impacted if the Company fails to comply with applicable government regulations, which can result in penalties or restrictions affecting operations.

Fluctuations in raw material prices may increase input costs, potentially affecting margins and profitability; the Company tracks commodity price trends and relies on volume-led growth, operational efficiencies and disciplined pricing actions to offset it.

Disruptions in global and local supply chains may lead to procurement delays, increased costs and profitability impact; mitigated through alternate sourcing, inventory planning and digital visibility tools.

Intense competition across product categories may restrict growth opportunities and pressure margins; the Company counters this via R&D-led product innovation, brand-equity investment and customer engagement.

Skilled manpower is critical for business growth; loss of key talent may affect operational efficiency and long-term sustainability, addressed through diversity, engagement programmes and continuous learning initiatives.

one-line thesis: This was a special update call (not a quarterly result) on Henkel's non-renewal of the Pril and Fa brand licenses, which ended on 31 May 2026. From 1 June 2026 Jyothy stopped all manufacturing, marketing, selling and distribution of both brands and has initiated arbitration at the Singapore International Arbitration Centre over the exit / transition / valuation mechanism. Pril was ~7–8% of total revenue (~₹225–240 cr) and the anchor in dishwash liquids; Fa's contribution was immaterial. Management pivots to scaling Exo Dishwash Liquid (in the portfolio since 2005-06) plus cross-category NPDs, and flags FY27 as a transition year with near-term margin softness.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy): No quarterly financials disclosed — this was an event call. Only the sizing of the affected business was given.

> Model note (per CFO): manufacturing/sales/distribution ran normally in April and May; primaries to ~3rd week of May, then only secondaries/tertiaries. Pril/Fa stopped 1 June — so ~2 months of Pril in FY27.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter: FY2027 = transition year for Dishwash Liquids; near-term impact on revenue mix and margins ("near-term margin softness").
No quantified recovery timeline for the lost Pril revenue despite repeated analyst probing — "we cannot comment on that... our efforts are there that we can make that happen sooner."
Recovery to come via Exo Liquid scale-up + NPDs across multiple categories over "the next few quarters."
Arbitration timing / outcome / quantum: explicitly refused — "very difficult to comment or speculate on legal outcome, timing... This is the first time that we have knocked the doors of SIAC."
Medium/long-term fundamentals "remain intact," supported by the diversified portfolio (Fabric Care, Home Care, Personal Care), distribution and manufacturing.
order book & pipeline: N/A (consumer FMCG — no order book). Demand levers cited: Exo's strong brand equity (No. 1 brand for the company, built in bars since 2001), enzymatic / antibacterial differentiation in both bars (first enzymatic bar in India) and the relaunched liquid, and pan-India distribution muscle "not dependent on one particular brand." NPD pipeline "across categories."
segment / subsidiary detail: Dishwash market structure: historically a ~2-player national market plus private labels; a few organized dishwash liquids exist "but they are not that big as of now." Pril = premium anchor in liquids; Exo = stronger franchise in bars (a "success story," the company's No.1 brand).

Exo Liquid: in the portfolio since 2005-06, then deprioritised post the 2011 Henkel acquisition (company chose Pril for liquids, Exo for bars). Now relaunched in Exo's 25th year; <1 quarter of data — "a very good welcome from distributors, market, consumers." Priced at par with the market leader (mid-mass, not low-end).
Fully owned: Margo, Neem Toothpaste, Tuhina, Chek.
Perpetual license, no royalty: Mr. White, Henko.
Fixed-term license (auto-renew every 5 yrs; renewed 2× over 10 yrs; ~2% royalty), defined exit provisions: Pril, Fa — now non-renewed.
Why Pril/Fa differed: Henkel operates Pril/Fa in other geographies globally (so kept them renewable), whereas Henko/Mr. White are not present elsewhere (hence perpetual).
growth verticals / optionality: Build Exo into a full-format dishwash franchise (bars + liquid) on an antibacterial/enzymatic platform.
NPDs across categories (not confined to dishwash) to "negate the gap" from the Pril/Fa exit.
Inorganic M&A optionality retained but discipline unchanged — the Pril/Fa exit "wouldn't put us in a situation where we will take any rash decision... constant lookout for the right fit."
margins & cost dynamics: Pril was premium-priced; Exo is priced at par with the market leader. Management argues India has "fewer takers for premium brands" and that a wider mass-priced reach beats a premium slot — no need to build a new premium liquid brand.
Dishwash-liquid margins are better than bars — a structural reason to push Exo Liquid.
FY27 margin softness during the transition; freed-up Pril A&P/capital redeployed behind Exo + NPDs.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): Manufacturing facilities are multiproduct and flexible → capacity can be redeployed across liquids and other growth categories. No material stranded manufacturing exposure from the Pril/Fa exit.
No new capex announced on this call.
capital allocation: A&P and capital previously behind Pril to be redeployed to Exo + cross-category NPDs.
Inorganic M&A stance unchanged — disciplined, no forced urgency from the exit.
Arbitration legal costs implied but unquantified; no comment on any contingent receivable/provision.
risks & watch-items: Revenue/margin hole: losing ~7–8% of revenue (Pril) from FY27; recovery pace unproven and unquantified.

Arbitration uncertainty: first-time SIAC/CIAC case; outcome, quantum and timing all unknown. Core dispute is not a single figure — it is the "proper treatment of end-of-term consequences... including the business transfer of Pril and Fa, brand-valuation consideration, and associated transition matters" (i.e., a combination of issues, including consideration linked to business momentum/goodwill created during the license period).
Execution risk on Exo Liquid (<1 quarter old) capturing the MT / e-commerce / premium shelf share Pril held.
Henkel's intent for the returned brands (re-launch itself vs sell-on to a new operator) — refused to speculate → potential future national competitor.
Compensation mechanics (sales multiple / EBITDA multiple / lump sum) not disclosed — "not explicitly mentioned in the agreement" per CFO; matter sub-judice.
management quality / tone: Measured and disciplined given sub-judice status; proactively hosted the call for transparency and set clear legal guardrails up front (no comment on claim amounts, valuation, timing or probability). CFO precise on the exit sequence and clean inventory/exposure position; CMD candid and confident on the Exo pivot without over-promising recovery timing. Repeatedly declined to speculate on distribution counts, arbitration timelines and Henkel's plans "for the right reasons."
non-obvious takeaways: Pril/Fa "behaved like long-term assets" thanks to 15 years of seamless 5-yearly auto-renewals and no recall signals — Jyothy effectively under-hedged the renewal risk; a contract-structure/governance lesson.
Exo Liquid was already in the portfolio (2005-06) and deliberately starved to protect Pril post-2011 — the pivot is a reactivation, not a from-scratch build.

The dispute is broader than a buy-back price — it centres on the exit mechanism plus goodwill/business-momentum-linked consideration → outcome could be a meaningful one-time receivable OR a drawn-out cost.
No royalty on Henko / Mr. White (perpetual) is a quietly valuable structural asset that survives this episode; only Pril/Fa carried royalty (~2%) and fixed-term risk.
Distribution is explicitly brand-agnostic ("go-to-market strategy is built on the whole basket") — management's key argument that no carry-forward channel damage flows to other brands.
qoq change log (fill each quarter): Q1FY27 (this, update call): Henkel non-renewed Pril & Fa; both exited 1 Jun 2026 (license term ended 31 May 2026); SIAC arbitration filed over exit/transition/valuation mechanism; Pril ~7–8% of revenue (~₹225–240 cr) lost, Fa immaterial; FY27 a dishwash-liquid transition year with near-term margin softness; strategy pivots to Exo Liquid (relaunched in its 25th year) + cross-category NPDs; no quantified recovery timeline; manufacturing flexible (no stranded capacity); no material residual inventory/receivable exposure as on 31 May 2026; inorganic M&A stance unchanged.

next Q → check: regular Q1FY27 results for actual Pril/Fa revenue & margin hit; Exo Liquid distribution/share traction; NPD launches; any arbitration update or contingent receivable/provision; whether HUL/private labels grabbed the vacated liquid share.

themes.title: Consumption revival & FMCG premiumization
themes.need: Rural recovery, GST 2.0 and premiumization still frame the theme, but Q1FY27 rewarded portfolio SHAPE over volume. TATACONSUM's growth businesses hit INR 1,300cr (+47%) and are now 36% of India - larger than either salt (>INR 1,000cr) or tea & coffee (INR 1,200cr), with Sampann +58%, RTD +41% and Capital Foods INR 232cr (+40%) - while India tea revenue fell 4% on +2% volume as lower tea costs were deliberately passed back (tea inflation is now running 7-10% with most buying still ahead, so that inverts next year). PGHH shows the margin route: FY26 sales roughly flat at ~INR 4,300cr but PAT +19% to ~INR 850cr and ~100bps of structural margin from INR 86cr of productivity savings, absorbing crude and resin each up 30-50% with no stock-outs. The cautionary tale is licensed brands - JYOTHYLAB lost the Pril and Fa licences when Henkel did not renew (all manufacturing and selling stopped 1-June; Pril was ~7-8% of revenue, ~INR 225-240cr) and has filed SIAC arbitration. MARICO/DABUR/GODREJCP/COLPAL/EMAMILTD ride distribution + premium mix; VBL on beverage route-to-market; BIKAJI/GOPAL/BECTORFOOD on branded snacks; ORKLAINDIA took a 4% blended price increase in Q4 plus premium mix to a 16.9% EBITDA margin.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull-through; rural volume recovery; festive/wedding restocking; commodity pass-back timing; JYOTHYLAB's ~7-8% revenue hole and the SIAC arbitration.

hero.oneLiner: A visionary Indian FMCG company with a strong consumer connect, holding market-leading positions in Fabric Care, Dishwashing and Household Insecticide categories.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: A visionary Indian FMCG company with a strong consumer connect, holding market-leading positions in Fabric Care, Dishwashing and Household Insecticide categories.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Jyothy Labs manufactures and markets Fast Moving Consumer Goods across Fabric Care, Dishwashing, Household Insecticide and Personal Care categories for Indian households, and through its Fabric Spa brand also provides laundry and dry-cleaning services. Products reach consumers pan-India (and in 19 countries via exports) through general trade, modern trade, e-commerce and quick-commerce channels.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- Jyothy Kallol Bangladesh Limited — subsidiary: Former subsidiary (control/significant influence existed) up to March 25, 2025; as on March 31, 2026 the Company has no subsidiary, associate or joint venture entities.
- Quilon Trading Co. — related party: Entity where Key Management Personnel and their relatives have significant influence.
- Jaya Trust — related party: Entity where Key Management Personnel and their relatives have significant influence.
- Sahyadri Bio Labs Private Limited — related party: Entity where Key Management Personnel and their relatives have significant influence.
- Sahyadri Agencies Ltd. — related party: Entity where Key Management Personnel and their relatives have significant influence.
- M. P. Ramachandran Family Trust - I — related party: Promoter group entity, w.e.f. April 25, 2025.
- M. P. Ramachandran Family Trust - II — related party: Promoter group entity, w.e.f. April 25, 2025.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body:
- **Dishwash:** Historically a ~2-player national market + private labels. Pril = anchor in **liquids** (premium-priced); Exo = stronger franchise in **bars** (since 2001), Exo Liquid existed since 2005-06 but was deprioritised in favour of Pril post-2011 Henkel acquisition. Exo Liquid recently **relaunched in Exo's 25th year**; <1 quarter of data, "good welcome" so far.
- **Brand ownership map (clarified):** Margo, Neem Toothpaste, Tuhina, Chek = **fully owned**. Mr. White, Henko = **perpetual license, no royalty**. Pril, Fa = **fixed-term license (auto-renew every 5 yrs, 2x renewed over 10 yrs), ~2% royalty** — now non-renewed.
- **Why Pril/Fa differed:** Henkel operates Pril/Fa in other geographies globally, so it kept renewable contracts; Henko/Mr. White not present elsewhere → perpetual.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Fabric Care:** Ujala (incl. Ujala Supreme), Henko, Morelight, Mr. White, Dr. Wool liquid detergent
- **Dishwashing:** Exo (bar and liquid formats), Pril (licensed from Henkel; licence not renewed beyond May 31, 2026)
- **Household Insecticide:** Maxo (mosquito repellent coil, aerosol, anti-mosquito racquet, liquid vaporisers)
- **Personal Care:** Margo, Jovia (beauty soap, new launch), Fa (licensed from Henkel; licence not renewed beyond May 31, 2026)
- **Others:** Fabric Spa (laundry and dry-cleaning services)

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Pan-India (national presence)
- 19 countries served via exports (~3.5% of FY26 turnover)
- Rural and semi-urban markets (via low unit packs / LUPs)
- Urban markets and modern trade, e-commerce and quick-commerce channels

order_book.title: Order book / demand drivers
order_book.body: N/A (consumer FMCG, no order book). Demand drivers cited: Exo brand equity (no. 1 brand for the company in bars), enzymatic/antibacterial differentiation in liquids, pan-India distribution muscle independent of any single brand.

guidance.title: Guidance (verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **FY2027 = transition year for Dishwash Liquids**; near-term hit to revenue mix and margins.
- No timeline given for arbitration outcome or recovery of lost Pril revenue ("cannot comment").
- Recovery to come via **Exo Liquid scale-up + NPDs across multiple categories** (next few quarters).
- No quantified revenue-recovery period despite repeated analyst probing.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- Exo as a **full-format dishwash franchise** (bars + liquids); enzymatic liquid + first enzymatic bar in India.
- **NPDs across categories** (not just dishwash) to fill the gap.
- Inorganic: "constant lookout for the right fit"; Pril/Fa exit will **not** force a rash deal; approach unchanged.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Demand recovery in H2 FY26 aided by GST rate cuts and relative resilience in rural markets (good monsoon and government spending)
- 2X growth in liquid detergents powered Fabric Care's outperformance (8.1% value growth, 9.5% volume growth) within the segment
- Dishwashing recorded 6% volume growth but a marginal 1.3% value decline, reflecting category-wide price corrections
- Household Insecticide segment losses narrowed on an improved mix led by Liquid Vaporisers and new formats, moving the segment towards profitability
- Raw material cost inflation could not be fully passed on to consumers, pressuring Gross Margin, EBITDA and PAT in FY26; geopolitical tensions added to the pressure
- Modern Trade, e-commerce and quick commerce channels grew 26% in FY26, becoming an increasingly important growth and new-customer-acquisition driver versus traditional trade
- For FY27, crude-linked input costs and geopolitical uncertainty may keep inflation elevated and affect consumer spending; rural demand may remain sensitive to farm incomes and monsoon outcomes
- Industry-level: urban FMCG volume growth (4.6% in 2025) outpaced rural (3.6%), while overall Indian FMCG volume growth slowed to 4.1% in 2025 from 4.7% in 2024
- GST 2.0 transition caused short-term disruption in Traditional Trade due to pricing/supply recalibration, while Modern Trade saw a sharp acceleration in Q3 FY26

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body:
- Pril was premium-priced; Exo priced at par with the market leader (mid-mass). Mgmt argues no need for a new premium brand — premium liquids have "fewer takers" and limited reach in India.
- Dishwash-liquid **margins are better**, a reason to push Exo Liquid.
- FY27 margin softness during transition; medium/long-term fundamentals intact.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Capital/A&P freed from Pril to be redeployed behind Exo + NPDs.
- Inorganic M&A optionality retained (disciplined, no urgency change).
- Arbitration costs implied but unquantified.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Jyothy Labs operates 23 manufacturing/processing facilities nationally (no international plants) supported by 32 depots and warehouses located pan-India and 3 R&D labs (Mumbai, Silvassa, Puducherry). The Company states capex on capacity expansion and upgradation of Rs 67 Crore during FY 2025-26, alongside continued investment in embracing advanced technologies and automation at its manufacturing units. On the sustainability/packaging side, during the year the Company completed the transition of the Exo Bar Rs 5 pack to a redesigned lightweight laminate, achieving an 11.3% reduction in plastic weight per unit versus the previous structure, and launched the new Exo Bar with Bio Enzymes range (3 variants) at the Rs 5 price point directly in this reduced-structure laminate. On energy, the Company reports a green solar energy capacity of 1,226 kW, renewable energy utilised of 15,60,056 kWh, and water savings of approximately 10% during FY26.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Measured and disciplined given sub-judice status; proactively hosted the call for transparency. Clear on legal guardrails (no comment on claim amounts/valuation/timing/probability). CFO precise on exposure/inventory clean-up; CMD candid on strategy pivot to Exo. Confident but did not over-promise recovery timing.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Market-leading brand positions: #1 Ujala Supreme in Fabric Whitener (since launch ~4 decades ago), #2 Exo Dishwash Bar in the Dishwash category by value, #2 Maxo Mosquito Repellent Coil by volume
- Wide direct distribution reach — 4 million outlets where products are available, 1.4 million outlets under direct reach, 10,000+ channel partners
- Net debt-free financial position with a substantial cash and bank balance (Rs 997 crore as of March 31, 2026), supporting continued investment capacity
- Sustained brand investment via high-profile multi-channel campaigns (brand ambassadors including Vidya Balan, Kareena Kapoor, Keerthy Suresh, Nayanthara, Raashii Khanna and Manju Warrier) across TV, digital and OOH
- Use of low unit packs (LUPs) to defend volume in rural/semi-urban markets against both unorganised local rivals and large competitors
- Growing presence in modern trade, e-commerce and quick commerce, which grew 26% in FY26, widening reach to new urban consumers
- R&D capability oriented towards green chemistry, automation and digital demand forecasting, supporting premiumisation and high-margin product development
- Recognised employer (Great Place to Work Certified Feb 2025-Feb 2026; among India's top 50 Best Workplaces in Manufacturing 2026 and Best Workplaces in FMCG 2025), aiding talent retention

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
- **Revenue/margin hole** from losing ~7–8% of sales (Pril) starting FY27; recovery pace unproven.
- **Arbitration uncertainty** — outcome, quantum and timing all unknown; first time at SIAC; core dispute = end-of-term treatment incl. business transfer + Pril/Fa brand valuation consideration + transition matters (not a single clean figure).
- Execution risk on Exo Liquid (sub-quarter old) gaining distribution/MT/e-com share Pril held.
- Henkel's intent for the returned brands (re-launch / sell-on) unknown → potential future competitor.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- Pril/Fa "behaved like long-term assets" due to 15-yr seamless auto-renewals — Jyothy under-hedged the renewal risk; a governance/contract-structure lesson.
- Exo Liquid was **already in the portfolio since 2005-06** and deliberately starved to protect Pril — so the pivot is a reactivation, not a from-scratch build.
- Dispute is broader than a simple buy-back price: it's about the **exit mechanism + goodwill/business-momentum-linked consideration** — outcome could be a meaningful one-time receivable OR a drawn-out cost.
- No royalty on Henko/Mr. White (perpetual) is a quietly valuable structural asset that survives this episode.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Continued strengthening of the core business by listening to consumers and responding with agility to evolving needs, backed by fiscal discipline and execution excellence
- Scaling up recent new product launches with greater focus on premium products, driving volume-led growth through innovation and distribution, supported by calibrated pricing
- Maintaining brand investment intensity by integrating it into disciplined financial planning, to sustain strong consumer recall in a competitive market
- Expanding direct retail reach (outlet additions) alongside deepening presence in Modern Trade, …

qoq_log.title: QoQ change log
qoq_log.body:
- **Q1FY27-Pril-Fa-Update (this):** Henkel non-renewed Pril & Fa; both exited 1 Jun 2026; SIAC arbitration filed; Pril ~7–8% of revenue (~₹225–240 cr) lost; FY27 a dishwash-liquid transition year with margin softness; strategy pivots to Exo Liquid + cross-category NPDs; no quantified recovery timeline; manufacturing flexible (no stranded capacity); inorganic stance unchanged.
- _next → check: regular Q1FY27 results for actual Pril/Fa revenue & margin hit; Exo Liquid distribution/share traction; NPD launches; any arbitration update or contingent receivable/provision; whether HUL/private labels grabbed the vacated liquid share._

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Segment restructure] Segment reporting moved from 5 segments (Fabric Care, Dishwashing, Household Insecticides, Personal Care, Others) to 3 segments (Fabric Care, Home Care, Personal Care); Laundry Service now sits inside Fabric Care, while Dishwashing, Household Insecticides and Other Products (incense sticks, Sambrani dhoop, floor cleaner, toilet cleaner) are consolidated into Home Care. The deck restates FY 25-26 revenue and result on both structures.
- [Portfolio change - Pril & Fa] The deck repeatedly footnotes "Pril & Fa upto 31st May 2026", removes After Shave, Deodorants and Talcum powder from the new Personal Care definition, and reports growth both with and without Pril; no reason for the cut-off is given anywhere in the deck.
- [Growth platforms] Way forward prioritises volume-led growth while protecting competitiveness, scaling recent NPDs including Exo Dishwash Liquid and Maxo Incense Sticks, and sharper pack-price and channel execution in Modern Trade, e-commerce and quick commerce.
- [Shareholding] As on 30th June 2026: Promoter and Promoter Group 62.89%, DII 14.21%, FII 12.72%, Public 10.18%.
